survey: A fruit plate on a wooden table, seen from about 40–45° above. The table planks run diagonally as parallel bands. They agree with that downward view and give no sign of a second camera. The plate is clear glass. Its rim is drawn as a true ellipse (about 0.65 height to width), its thickness shows only along the near edge, and it lies flat on the planks. On the plate: a watermelon wedge stands upright with its cut face toward the viewer. Because that face is vertical, seeing it nearly front-on is correct for this camera. Its seeds follow the curve of the flesh, and its rind wraps along the bottom and right edge. An orange half leans against the wedge at the right, with its cut face turned toward the viewer as a slightly narrowed circle, which suits a face tilted toward the camera. An orange wedge in front lies on its peel with its cut face up and forward. A cluster of green grapes sits in the middle, drawn as a rounded pile seen slightly from above. Strawberries (leaves seen from above) and blueberries (crown openings seen at an angle) sit around the front edge. Water drops lie on the plate surface. Every piece rests on the plate's surface, and the near pieces overlap the front rim the way they should.
